    //==
    // # What the layered mesh vocabulary derives for free
    //
    // The bodies an implementor of `meshes.concepts.plato` does not have to
    // write. An indexed geometry declares its vertex pool and its index table; the
    // point view then follows from the pool, because for indexed storage the shape's
    // points ARE the pool. (That is not true one layer down: an unwelded soup has no
    // pool, and its Points are the flattened corners of its primitives, so the soups
    // supply Points themselves in the face-array section below.)
    //
    // `Primitives` is deliberately NOT derived here. Gathering an index tuple into a
    // concrete primitive needs that primitive's constructor, which the generic layer
    // cannot name, so each named binding supplies its own one-line gather.

    // The IPointGeometry obligation of any indexed geometry: the shared vertex
    // pool is exactly the set of points the shape is built from.
    Points(self: IIndexedGeometry<$TPoint, $TPrim, $TIndex>): Array<$TPoint>
        => self.Vertices;

    //==
    // # Deformation bodies for line sets and bare point clouds
    //
    // The IDeformable2D/IDeformable3D obligations of the face-free geometry in
    // `meshes.types.plato`: every stored position is carried through the
    // mapping; the segment index pairs are pure connectivity and pass through
    // unchanged.

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: every vertex position carried through the
    // mapping, segment pairs unchanged.
    Deform(self: LineSet3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): LineSet3D
        => (self.Positions.Map(mapping), self.Lines);

    // The IDeformable2D obligation: every vertex position carried through the
    // mapping, segment pairs unchanged.
    Deform(self: LineSet2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): LineSet2D
        => (self.Positions.Map(mapping), self.Lines);

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: every position carried through the mapping.
    Deform(self: PointCloud3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): PointCloud3D
        => PointCloud3D(self.Positions.Map(mapping));

    // The IDeformable2D obligation: every position carried through the mapping.
    Deform(self: PointCloud2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): PointCloud2D
        => PointCloud2D(self.Positions.Map(mapping));

    //==
    // # The indexed-segment layer

    // The IIndexedGeometry obligations: the shared pool and the segment table.
    Vertices(self: LineSet3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.Positions;

    FaceIndices(self: LineSet3D): Array<VertexPair>
        => self.Lines;

    // The IPrimitiveGeometry obligation: each pair gathered into a concrete
    // segment, in authored direction.
    Primitives(self: LineSet3D): Array<Line3D>
        => self.Lines.Map(e => Line3D(self.Positions[e.A.Value],
                                      self.Positions[e.B.Value]));

    Vertices(self: LineSet2D): Array<Point2D>
        => self.Positions;

    FaceIndices(self: LineSet2D): Array<VertexPair>
        => self.Lines;

    // The IPrimitiveGeometry obligation, in the plane.
    Primitives(self: LineSet2D): Array<Line2D>
        => self.Lines.Map(e => Line2D(self.Positions[e.A.Value],
                                      self.Positions[e.B.Value]));

    //==
    // # Deformation body for the partitioned mesh
    //
    // The IDeformable3D obligation of SegmentedMesh3D (`meshes.types.plato`):
    // deformation moves positions and never reorders faces, so the section table —
    // face ranges and slots — passes through unchanged.

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: the underlying mesh deformed, the section
    // partition unchanged.
    Deform(self: SegmentedMesh3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): SegmentedMesh3D
        => (self.Mesh.Deform(mapping), self.Sections);

    // The IMesh3D obligation: the geometry without its section partition.
    // The face order is the partition's order, so a caller that wants to keep
    // the grouping reads Sections alongside this.
    ToTriangleMesh(self: SegmentedMesh3D): TriangleMesh3D
        => self.Mesh;

    //==
    // # Derived functionality for mesh connectivity
    //
    // Pure, expression-bodied helpers for the interfaces declared in
    // `topology.concepts.plato` (IMeshElementCounts, IMeshIncidence,
    // IHalfEdge). Part of P8 of the interface library.
    //
    // The three sections follow the interface ladder: what counts alone can tell you,
    // what incidence adds, and what a built half-edge structure adds. Each helper
    // sits on the weakest rung that can answer it — the valence of a vertex needs
    // incidence but not half-edges, so it is written once, there.
    //
    // Lower-package generics are reused, not re-declared: Integer counts are `IWhole`,
    // so P1's `IsZero`/`IsPositive`/`IsNegative` apply directly; typed element
    // indices are `IIndex`, so P2's `IsNone`/`IsPresent` express "-1 means none"
    // without touching `.Value`.

    //==
    // IMeshElementCounts — counted mesh elements: vertices, undirected edges,
    // faces. All derived facts follow from the three counts and the Euler
    // relation. Nothing here can see connectivity, so nothing here can check
    // the closed/connected/manifold preconditions its formulas need.

    // The Euler characteristic V - E + F
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_characteristic). A closed connected
    // manifold of genus g has Euler characteristic 2 - 2g; a disk has 1, a sphere
    // 2, a torus 0.
    EulerCharacteristic(self: IMeshElementCounts): Integer
        => self.VertexCount - self.UndirectedEdgeCount + self.FaceCount;

    // The genus implied by the Euler characteristic, valid ONLY for a closed,
    // connected, 2-manifold surface: genus = (2 - EulerCharacteristic) / 2
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus_(mathematics)).
    // Integer division truncates; the precondition guarantees an even numerator.
    GenusIfClosed(self: IMeshElementCounts): Integer
        => (2 - self.EulerCharacteristic) / 2;

    // True when the mesh has no vertices (hence no edges or faces).
    IsEmpty(self: IMeshElementCounts): Boolean
        => self.VertexCount.IsZero;

    // True when the mesh carries at least one face.
    HasFaces(self: IMeshElementCounts): Boolean
        => self.FaceCount.IsPositive;

    // True when the mesh carries at least one undirected edge.
    HasUndirectedEdges(self: IMeshElementCounts): Boolean
        => self.UndirectedEdgeCount.IsPositive;

    // True for a non-empty mesh that carries vertices but no faces: a point set
    // or wireframe. An empty mesh is neither, so it returns false.
    IsPointsOrWireframe(self: IMeshElementCounts): Boolean
        => self.IsEmpty.Not.And(self.HasFaces.Not);

    //==
    // IMeshIncidence — which elements touch which
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incidence_matrix). These are the
    // neighbourhood facts that do NOT need a stored adjacency structure, only
    // the ability to answer the six incidence queries. An empty result is the
    // "none" answer, so the local classifications below read off array lengths.

    // The number of vertices bounding a face: its arity.
    // Precondition: the face is present.
    FaceVertexCount(self: IMeshIncidence, face: FaceIndex): Integer
        => self.VerticesOfFace(face).Count;
